description: How the Campaigns screen says where a race stands: voters reached, how many warmed or cooled, who the opponents are, the last poll and what a poll costs. Every part is a whole sentence; the facts are slots from the campaign's cause, filing and poll records and the Poll action's price. The volunteer asks say each answer: yes (the person signs on) or no (they cannot help just now), from the volunteer ask's answer.

slots.reached: Voters reached, from the campaign's cause records (each voter once).
slots.warmer: Voters whose warmth toward the candidate rose, from the same records.
slots.cooler: Voters whose warmth fell, from the same records.
slots.opponents: The other candidates on the contest's filing records.
slots.name: One candidate on the contest's filing records.
slots.sample: The poll's sample size, from the Poll action.
slots.cost: Dollars the poll costs: sample times the campaign engine's price per interview.
slots.date: The date the poll was taken.
slots.tally: Each answer with its count, from the poll record.
slots.amount: Dollars given, from the gift row and journal entry.
slots.gave: How many people gave on this call.
slots.asked: How many people were asked on this call.
slots.office: The seat as people say it ("a seat on the Mutual Village Council", "mayor"), from the contest and office records through the one seat reader.
slots.closes: The day filing closes, while it is still ahead, from the contest's filing deadline.
slots.raised: Dollars the campaign has raised in all, from the campaign record.
slots.cash: Dollars the campaign holds now (raised less spent), from the campaign record.
slots.filed: The day the player filed, as people say a date, from the filing record.
slots.general: The general election's day, as people say a date, from the contest record, once the primary is past or where there is none.
slots.primary: The primary's day, as people say a date, from the contest record, while it is ahead.
